blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Supreme Court has dismissed two petitions challenging the Senate Impeachment Court’s ruling on the voting threshold required to convict Vice President Sara Duterte. Former Executive Secretary Vic Rodriguez and lawyer Ernesto Francisco Jr. filed separate petitions seeking judicial intervention after the Senate adjusted the constitutional two-thirds voting requirement. The petitions were dismissed due to procedural lapses. Rodriguez, in his 23-page Petition for Certiorari and Prohibition filed Sept. 24, argued that the Senate chamber’s ruling had unlawfully rewritten the 1987 Constitution.
